title: The Three Al's trio and the Buckaroo job
summary: He recalls the Three Al's with Albert Burbank and Albert Giles, and a job at the Buckaroo with Charlie Hamilton.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Maybe we better go back and ask you some questions. Yeah, he wanted to ask you some questions. Yeah, I wanted to hear about that Three Al's trio. It was you and Albert Boybanks and Albert John, right?
The Three Al's. When was that?

Well, three Al's, Albert Boybanks, we used to, where were we playing? We had, you know, Albert Boybanks was playing clarinet and Albert Giles was playing drums. We was playing at, down on St. Louis and Wisconsin. When was that?
That must have been a long time ago. Yeah. Baby Green's evening and- On that side, but Baby Green was, I don't know who was, we was playing that for a while,
and then we was playing back, I'm trying to think.
That was a group you had for a long time?
Yeah, we had that group. Yeah. You're just bringing things to me. Yeah. I was with that group too.

That was right after, let me see, that was around 40, I remember we had another group before that, but I'll get back to that. We was working at Buckaroo with this man, Charlie Hamilton was playing piano, and Old Man James was playing alto sax, and Brady was playing drums.
Old Man James that played bass, he was playing alto? Yeah, playing alto.

His brother played alto. Squeak's daddy, his brother died, went to California and died, his brother played alto. We used to work for St. Charles, Louis James' brother. And then we left- You had Brady on? Well Brady was drums. Which Brady? Brady the drum player, I don't know, you sure? Brady Smith, yeah. Yeah, Brady Smith was playing drums, Charlie Hamilton was playing piano. Charlie Hamilton got that car when he drives his day, he made that offer tipsy board off of that job with Buckaroo, St. Charles. St. James. Yeah, right after the war, that was around 40, after we left the Royal Rondeville with Patterson, that's right. I went up there working with that bunch, and after that job pulled up, then I went with Boybanks.
